debrief_text.analysis: The anchor's mechanics are new to this module, and the difference is the lesson. Case 4's anchor was installed by another clinician before the learner arrived; case 5's was installed by the learner's own true history at stage 1. This one is installed MID-CASE, by a test result: the BNP returns at stage 2 — a true number, honestly weighed by the workbench itself, which also moves heart failure up (0.12 to 0.2881) — and the learner converts a rising differential into a settled diagnosis ('the BNP is up, the legs are swollen, it's her heart'), then reads every later result inside the frame: the wide A-a gradient becomes 'fluid', the measured calf becomes 'post-op swelling' (on the un-operated side), the troponin becomes 'demand'. Note what the frame survives: a completed Wells score of 6.0 on the case's own declared block, and a CTPA showing bilateral emboli — the learner still holds heart failure at 0.16 at stage 3, the stage the workbench rules it out at 0.0041. The counterweights were all mechanical, which is the case's thesis: a score completed from atoms cannot be argued with the way a gestalt can, a tape measure outranks an impression of 'swollen legs', and a peptide that rises in right-sided strain cannot arbitrate between the ventricles. The closing symmetry is deliberate: the test that ends the anchor is the one the learner ordered to confirm it.
debrief_text.description: Stage 1: a post-operative dyspnoea with a board led, reasonably, by embolism (0.22) over heart failure (0.20) — the two frames are both alive and the learner's numbers are defensible. Stage 2: the BNP returns at 385 and the learner's board inverts — heart failure 0.42, embolism down to 0.18 — while the workbench, applying the same BNP weight, keeps embolism ahead (0.3790 to 0.2881) because it also weighs the D-dimer and cannot un-measure the calf. Stage 3: the CTPA is decisive for the workbench (0.9554) and nearly so for the learner (0.78), but heart failure is still held at 0.16 — the anchoring event the machinery records, the only one in the attempt. Stage 4: the commit is correct and the residual heart-failure mass (0.05) is below the anchoring line: the frame is released, a stage late and after its own test refuted it.
debrief_text.reactions: The learner's stage-2 inversion is the most human board in this module so far: a single famous number arriving in a batch of quieter ones. Nothing he ordered was wrong — the stage-1 panel is the right panel, the CTPA is placed the moment the score completes, and the lung ultrasound is a genuinely good test. The failure is purely interpretive, and it is scored as such.
debrief_text.summary: Acute dyspnoea twelve days after joint replacement is a vascular presentation until the evidence retires it. Complete the score from atoms before weighing the biomarkers; measure the calves; remember that BNP reports ventricular strain, not ventricular identity; and when your own confirmatory test contradicts your frame, believe the test.

commit.management: Admission to a monitored bed; anticoagulation for intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism on the ESC 2019 risk-adjusted strategy; no thrombolysis while haemodynamically stable; no Theatre handoff — the Theatre holds no pulmonary embolism procedure, as the case's management block records.
